value.rationale: Critical habitat size is a natural ecological extinction-threshold invariant of stochastic relocation. At fixed relocation spread (mean and variance), the theorem completely classifies the best and worst spatial relocation policies and proves a rate-controlled reversal with an exact distribution-independent critical point. The result is not merely a new numerical parameter or relabeling of an existing fixed-reset formula: its unique extremal measures and sign-switch use nontrivial convex-order structure over all probability laws.
